properties.notes: Layered granitic intrusion - granite to granophyre layers.
Slaufling sill
Slaufey sill - vesicular, fine-grained, aphanitic. Felsite, likley rhyolite, my be crypto-intrusive.
Birnugil intrusion

Simplified for map scale. A complex formation consisting of distinct units of sediment, pyroclastic rocks and cross cut by intrusions. Overlain by the Dalsheiði palagonite breccia. Fossil bearing (trace fossils).
Large rhyolite body
Forms a 'cap' unit for the pluton
Welded, fiamme bearing - black to white, some sections more welded than others. Outcrop not accessible on day of visit except one exposure of black, glassy (poorly) ignimbrite.

Layered unit, reworked mafic volcaniclastic, and pyroclastic units, mapped seperately as it overlies the rhyolite lava. Though appears to interfinger with ignimbrites to the south - no contact exposures.
aerial imagery mapped
Orange-pink ignimbrite. Likely connects with the very similar unit to the north in Afdalur.
Fine grained rhyolite intrusion
Rhyolite sill
Dyke in E-W fracture. Granitic. Likely related to the pluton.
Lithic rich intrusion, angular lithics with no reaction rims - mechanical fracturing. Granite and gabbro clasts. Granite fuidal - thermally reacting. Conduit ignimbrite.

Welded ignimbrite, confined morphology likely a conduit. Displays highly variable morphology within the small unit - some sections with fiamme, others clastic (angular lithics) in glass, and some welded or sintered sections.
Massive rhyolite - inaccessible
Plagioclase porphyrytic unit
Plagioclase porhyrytic
Mafic tuff, altered.
Layered tuff unit with subunits of ignimbrite, tuff, reworked voclaniclastic.
Gabbroic section within a confined outcrop in Þorgeirs. Likely related to the pluton.

A very hard unit, in the field its hardness is indistinguisable from the basalts around it. Noted for its fluvial features, layering, cross-bedding and some round "burrow-like" features in sandstone layers.
Rhyolite intrusion, exposire inaccessible, appears to trace along a fracture feature which may relate to Skeggil fault

Porrly exposed ignimbrite, best exposure along intrusion contact where it is somewhat hardened. Lithic rich ignimbrite with pumice clasts. Likely traces further than mapped extent but lack of exposure and structural data negates further inference.

Likely not a single unit as the sediment (some outcrops breccia, others lithic bearing sandstone) appears to be interupted by lavas though the oxposure is poor and confined to small (<2 m) outcrops along the sill boundary.
Vesicular, flow foliated rhyolite. No lithics, likely a lava flow (welded lava-like ignimbrite possible but no clasts or fiamme seen).
Hihgly altered (chlorite) pumice breccia, in some areas pumice clasts are sintered to the glass matrix. Contains angular clasts of coarse granitic material (altered).

Thick unit. Variable, needs more work. Massive, poorly bedded to unbedded, some sections display faint layering. Clastic, poorly sorted (type and cm-dm sized), angular to sub angular, matrix altered-fine. R. Gupta found evidence of primary pyroclaastics. Mixed mass flow deposit.

Basaltic, consisting of clasts - monomictic, the matrix is the same material as the blocks. Matrix is coarse sand to fine gravel at its finest, alteration minerals infill voids. Interp: volcanic debris flow - probably primary, e.g. collapse into a valley.

Sedimentary unit consisting of subfacies of Conglomerate containing basaltic lithics, overlain by red sandstone, aphyric basalt lava, and a sequence of well sorted breccia containing subangular clasts of basalt. Lateral extant unknown.
Altered sedimentary unit. Not mapped in detail
Silicic sheet, sub horizontal, bounding upper part of the Kapaldaur tuff formation
So named after Steffi's slide down ball bearing scree.
From virtual outcrop mapping
From virtual outcrop mapping
Likely related to the Laxárdalur sheet according to aerial imagery
Plateau basalts, interbeds, including some thin fluvial units. Mostly altered to chlorite-epitode facies.
Inaccessible except by the ridge to the north, needs proper observations. Scree samples indicate a red, vesicular rhyolite. The outcrop is extensive, forming much of the mountaintop. Rhyolite lava.
Mapped by Torfasson as hyaloclastite. Upon revisiting this outcrop I observed a poorly exposed breccia between basalt lavas, suggest it may be sedimentary.
NULClastic rock with white fiamme (replaced with secondary alteration)

Mapped as one formation for map scale. A highly complex formation of multiple units of pyrocastic rocks and breccias. In general contisting of lithic rich ignimbrites but also seen are sintered ignimbrites, welded ignimbrites and tuffs.
Mafic intrusion through breccia
Outcrop above kvosafoss, structural contours indicate linking with hvammsheipi and slufrudalur porphyrytic groups.
Inferred unit trace
Altered unit, clastic with an ash/sandstone matrix. Too altered to see internal features.
Conglomerate, poor exposure though some sedimentary features visible. Fluvial.
Poorly exposed in river bed. Clastic boundary, likely clastic lava (a'a).
Layered granitic intrusion - granite to granophyre layers.
Steffi mapping
Likely much larger but not able to trace further
Volcanic and sedimentary breccias, layered, complex and high angle of deposition.
Mixing and mingling zone, both granite and gabbro in a close relationship.
Both gabbro and the mixing complex
